about: Nodes of the meteorology lineage graph, type "site": what people look at. Ids are stable (incident.entities@ may adopt them); meaning is in the edges (meteorology/edges/), not here.

nodes.name: IPMA
nodes.summary: Home: the map of warnings by district with a day selector, the forecast for the capitals, the latest communiqués and the seismic map.

nodes.name: Windy
nodes.summary: A full-screen animated map (wind particles over a colour field) with a layer menu (wind, gusts, rain, waves, pressure), a model switch (ECMWF, GFS, ICON, AROME) and a time slider along the bottom.

nodes.name: Ventusky
nodes.summary: Animated map like Windy, with a strong gust layer and fronts drawn on the map.

nodes.name: earth.nullschool.net
nodes.summary: The globe with flowing wind lines (GFS), minimal chrome: the picture is the page.

nodes.name: Zoom Earth
nodes.summary: Near-real-time satellite imagery with a time scrubber; radar, wind and pressure layers.

nodes.name: Yr (MET Norway and NRK)
nodes.summary: A place page with one table: a row per day that opens into a row per hour (symbol, temperature, precipitation in mm, wind speed with an arrow and the wind in words).

nodes.name: meteoblue
nodes.summary: Lisbon read: a 7-day strip with predictability per day as a percentage.

nodes.name: The Weather Channel (weather.com)
nodes.summary: Place card (now, feels like, high/low), hourly and 10-day, radar map, video.

nodes.name: AccuWeather
nodes.summary: Not opened (403). Known for minute-by-minute precipitation and its own impact scales.

nodes.name: BBC Weather
nodes.summary: A place page that is one horizontal strip: day tabs across the top, under them an hour-by-hour row (symbol, temperature, chance of precipitation, wind arrow with speed.

nodes.name: Weather Underground
nodes.summary: A network of personal weather stations on a map (Lisbon has many), each with its own page and history graph.

nodes.name: Meteociel

nodes.name: Luso Meteo

nodes.name: Observador
nodes.summary: Live blog (general news) and a long special on Charles with embedded gust maps.

nodes.name: US National Weather Service
nodes.summary: A national hazards map coloured by warning type with a legend ordered by priority.

nodes.name: US National Hurricane Center
nodes.summary: One map of the basin with every active system; per storm a fixed set of products issued on a fixed clock (public advisory, forecast advisory, discussion, wind-speed probabilities) and the cone graphic: the track, the forecast points with times, the uncertainty cone, the coastal warnings.

nodes.name: Deutscher Wetterdienst (Germany)
nodes.summary: Warnings map down to municipality level with a time slider; the WarnWetter app.

nodes.name: Météo-France: Vigilance
nodes.summary: The vigilance map: one colour per département, tabs for today and tomorrow, the issue time and the validity on the card, the time the next map is due, a legend written as actions, maps per phenomenon, and one bar per phenomenon along the hours of the day.

nodes.name: AEMET (Spain)
nodes.summary: Warnings map by zone with tabs for today, tomorrow and the day after and a table of every warning (zone, phenomenon, level, start, end, probability, comment).

nodes.name: KNMI (Netherlands)
nodes.summary: Home leads with the colour code for the country and a one-paragraph "weather picture" by the duty forecaster.

nodes.name: SMHI (Sweden)
nodes.summary: Impact-based warnings (the same wind gets a different level by region and season), each with "what can happen".

nodes.name: Finnish Meteorological Institute
nodes.summary: Local forecast with an hourly table and a 5-day warnings strip per region.

nodes.name: Japan Meteorological Agency
nodes.summary: One "disaster prevention" map application with every layer on the same base map (warnings, typhoon track and probability circle, rain nowcast, river flood and landslide risk meshes), in 15 languages.

nodes.name: Bureau of Meteorology (Australia)
nodes.summary: Redesigned home: a place card first (now, today, the next hours), then warnings for that place, then the radar.

nodes.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada
nodes.summary: Alerts map and table; city pages with text forecast and hourly table.

nodes.name: MeteoSwiss
nodes.summary: Home is the map with an animation bar (past radar into forecast, one continuous timeline).

nodes.name: Met Éireann (Ireland)
nodes.summary: Warnings first on the home page as a list with status, validity and issue time.

nodes.name: MeteoAlarm
nodes.summary: One map of Europe coloured by the highest warning per region, from the national services themselves.

nodes.name: WMO Severe Weather Information Centre
nodes.summary: World map of official warnings and tropical cyclones from national services, in CAP.

nodes.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service
nodes.summary: Rapid mapping activations (satellite damage and flood extent maps) and EFAS flood forecasts.

nodes.name: Open-Meteo
nodes.summary: A free JSON API over the open models of the national services (ECMWF, DWD ICON, Météo-France AROME/ARPEGE, and others), hourly, any point, with gusts.

nodes.name: European Severe Weather Database
nodes.summary: Quality-controlled reports of severe weather events (wind, tornado, hail, rain) on a map.

nodes.name: FU Berlin: Aktion Wetterpate
nodes.summary: Names every low and high over Europe (a second, older naming scheme).

nodes.name: IPMA: radar, satellite, stations, lightning
nodes.summary: Radar mosaic with animation; satellite (Meteosat channels); hourly surface observations with graphs per station.

nodes.name: CNN Portugal / TVI: video coverage and "Por onde vai entrar a tempestade Charles"

nodes.name: Correio da Manhã / CMTV: "Veja o percurso da tempestade Charles"

nodes.name: Wikipedia (pt): "Depressão Charles"

nodes.summary: No article of its own in English ("Storm Charles 2026" does not exist).

nodes.summary: A presenter-led video forecast in English (17:35Z) and two earlier text items.
